title: What actually triggers SICR: building a Stage 2 test you can defend
dek: Thirty days past due is the backstop, not the test. How to design a significant increase in credit risk assessment that moves loans early, behaves sensibly across the rating scale, and leaves an audit trail for every exposure.
summary: Why a fixed PD multiple behaves differently at each end of the rating scale, what the demo book's trigger mix looks like, and how far the allowance moves when the threshold changes.

title: From transition matrix to forward-looking lifetime PD
dek: How to build IFRS 9 lifetime PD curves that are traceable from end to end: compounding a rating matrix, turning macro scenarios into one credit cycle index, shifting hazard rates, and why the probability-weighted allowance is higher than the baseline.
summary: Compounding a transition matrix into PD curves, building a credit cycle index from four macro variables, and why the weighted allowance sits 24% above the baseline in the demo book.

title: Stress testing capital from the loan book
dek: A stressed loss rate answers one supervisory question. This note covers the follow-ups: migration as well as default, the RWA inflation that downgrades cause, the CET1 bridge a board can read, and a reverse stress test expressed in numbers rather than prose.
summary: Migration, RWA inflation, the CET1 bridge and a reverse stress test in numbers, worked through on the demo bank, where the severe scenario leaves 0.73 points of headroom.
